question: A 48-year-old man presents with melaena and syncope. His systolic BP is 90 mmHg, pulse 112 bpm, haemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, and serum urea 14 mmol/L. He has no known cardiac disease. Which scoring system is MOST appropriate to determine whether he can be safely discharged without endoscopy?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The pre-endoscopy Rockall Score assesses re-bleeding risk and mortality but does NOT predict which patients can be safely managed without endoscopy — that is the specific purpose of the Glasgow-Blatchford Score.

Correct. The Glasgow-Blatchford Score (GBS) uses clinical and biochemical parameters (BUN, haemoglobin, systolic BP, pulse, syncope, melaena, hepatic disease, cardiac failure) to identify patients who need intervention. A GBS of 0 identifies low-risk patients safe for outpatient management.
AIMS65 predicts inpatient mortality in UGIB but is not designed to stratify need for endoscopy or guide discharge decisions — that role belongs to the Glasgow-Blatchford Score.

The Forrest Classification describes endoscopic appearances of peptic ulcers and their re-bleeding risk — it is applied AFTER endoscopy, not before it. It cannot be used to decide whether endoscopy is needed.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the risk stratification section. The Glasgow-Blatchford Score is specifically designed for pre-endoscopy triage of UGIB, while the Rockall Score assesses re-bleeding risk and is completed after endoscopy.
Well done. The Glasgow-Blatchford Score is the validated pre-endoscopy tool for identifying patients who require intervention — a GBS of 0 is the only validated threshold to safely defer endoscopy.
